def: An open platform-independent communication architecture standardized in IEC 62541 using TCP port 4840, PKI with X.509v3 certificates, and hierarchical address spaces.
A software layer that sits between the operating system and user applications to provide common communication, data serialization, and device abstraction.
Stochastic odometry errors caused by unpredictable terrain-wheel interactions (such as wheel slip or floor irregularities) that vary randomly between runs.
A PROFINET communication class that bypasses TCP/IP layers to achieve deterministic communication in the 1 to 10 millisecond range.
A mathematical model of computation consisting of a discrete set of states, input events, transitions, and actions where an entity resides in exactly one state at a time.
A dual full-bridge motor driver IC utilizing bipolar junction transistors (BJTs), characterized by a 1.8V to 3.2V internal voltage drop and high thermal dissipation.
The formal standard term designating that safety is a characteristic of the complete robotic task, tooling, and environment, rather than the arm alone.
A compact mathematical representation of 3D orientation where the vector direction defines the rotation axis and its length defines the angle in radians.
ROS Middleware Interface, the internal C abstraction layer that decouples higher-level ROS 2 client libraries from specific underlying DDS or Zenoh implementations.
Simultaneous Localization and Mapping, the computational process of constructing a map of an unknown environment while tracking a robot's location within it.
Deterministic odometry errors caused by physical vehicle parameters (such as unequal wheel diameters or wheelbase uncertainty) that repeat identically across runs.
A managed ROS 2 node that transitions through a formal state machine (Unconfigured, Inactive, Active, Finalized) for deterministic system startup.
A document that establishes ground rules for participant behavior to facilitate a friendly, welcoming environment across a project.
A supervisory system architecture requiring affirmative human confirmation before an automated robot can execute high-consequence decisions.
A high-level, Pascal-derived programming language used on FANUC controllers for complex calculations, communications, and background logic.
ABB's motion optimization algorithm that dynamically calculates maximum possible acceleration and deceleration without overloading mechanical joints.
A visual hierarchical representation of robot program logic, motion waypoints, and conditionals in PolyScope.
A synchronous or asynchronous request-and-response communication mechanism between two ROS nodes for discrete transactions.
The algorithmic process of combining sensory data derived from disparate sources such that the resulting information has less uncertainty than when sources are used individually.
A formal test of a finished robot cell at the integrator's site before it ships, checking build quality, controls, safety logic and basic performance.
Pulsing an LED light source with brief microsecond bursts synchronized to camera exposure, reducing heat and allowing high-current overdriving to freeze fast motion.
A specialized optical lens with chief rays parallel to the optical axis, eliminating parallax error and maintaining constant magnification across varying object distances.
The OPC UA Companion Specification for Robotics defining a standardized information model for asset management, condition monitoring, and preventive maintenance across robot brands.
Windows Subsystem for Linux version 2, a lightweight virtualization architecture that runs a real Linux kernel and GUI applications seamlessly on Windows 11.
Inertial Measurement Unit; an integrated electronic package combining 3-axis MEMS accelerometers, 3-axis gyroscopes, and optional magnetometers to measure body motion and orientation.
A popular open-source microcontroller development board widely used for robotics prototyping, available in 8-bit AVR (R3) and 32-bit Arm (R4) architectures.
Sequential Function Chart; a graphical programming language standardized under IEC 61131-3 for industrial programmable logic controllers (PLCs) based on Petri nets.
An IEEE 802 standards family designed to provide deterministic connectivity with bounded latency, low packet delay variation, and low packet loss.
The updated international safety standard (Parts 1 and 2) specifying requirements for industrial robots, robotic systems, and collaborative cell integration.
Weighted average calculations of image pixel intensities used to determine geometric properties such as area, orientation, and centroid coordinates.
A horizontal international standard series defining requirements and processes for implementing and maintaining secure industrial automation and control systems.
A low-level programming language in which each instruction corresponds closely to one machine instruction of a specific processor.
A preemptible, long-running goal-oriented communication pattern in ROS that provides periodic progress feedback and a final result.
The ROS Enhancement Proposal documenting supported operating systems, architectures, and compiler standards for each ROS 2 distribution.
The precise physical measurement of part dimensions—such as lengths, diameters, and clearances—from calibrated camera image coordinates.
The economic counter-mechanism where technological advancement generates entirely new tasks, roles, and occupations requiring human labor.
The covariance representing statistical uncertainty, electronic noise, and quantization errors inherent to a physical sensor.

A functional safety networking design where safety and standard communication integrate on one transmission medium by treating the underlying network as unreliable and placing diagnostics entirely in end devices.
A component in the ros2_control framework that connects controllers with the hardware abstraction interface.

The international standard that defines robotics vocabulary; its 2021 edition defines a robot as a programmed actuated mechanism with a degree of autonomy to perform locomotion, manipulation or positioning.
An acoustic disturbance caused by magnetostriction and coil vibration in motors when driven at PWM frequencies within human hearing range (20 Hz to 20 kHz).
A globally standardized point-to-point IO technology under IEC 61131-9 for communicating with sensors and actuators using standard three-wire cables and M12, M8, or M5 connectors.
Random Sample Consensus; an iterative mathematical algorithm that estimates model parameters from data containing a high proportion of outliers, commonly used to detect geometric planes.
A self-operating machine, such as Hero of Alexandria's temple doors or Jaquet-Droz's writing doll, that moves by itself following a built-in mechanism (plural: automata).
Bidirectional Synchronous Serial Interface, an open, bidirectional serial protocol for absolute encoders: the controller can read position and also read and write encoder memory.
The horizontal pixel displacement between corresponding object points in the left and right images of a calibrated stereo camera pair, inversely proportional to depth.
The requirement in international law and ethics that human operators maintain situational awareness, legal agency, and veto capability over autonomous military weapon systems.
An instruction manual that welcomes community members, explains why the project is useful, and provides getting started instructions, descriptions, and usage examples.
The discrepancy between a robot's simulated performance in CAD and its actual physical motion due to manufacturing tolerances, deflection, and fixture offsets.
A placeholder in a launch file, such as LaunchConfiguration or FindPackageShare, whose value is only worked out when the launch actually runs.
The University of Michigan Benchmark; a standardized calibration procedure driving clockwise and counter-clockwise square paths to decouple wheel diameter and wheelbase errors.
An illumination technique placing the light source behind the object to create a high-contrast opaque silhouette for boundary and dimensional inspection.
A ROS 2 QoS policy that transmits messages without acknowledgment or retransmission, prioritizing low latency and data freshness over packet loss.
A three-term closed-loop feedback control algorithm calculating corrective actuation based on proportional error, accumulated past error, and error rate of change.
The number of operational industrial robots per 10,000 employees in the manufacturing sector, tracked globally by the International Federation of Robotics.
An ABB RAPID data structure storing a robot target position in millimeters, orientation as a quaternion, axis configurations, and external axes.
The ROS 2 workspace or installation (such as /opt/ros/lyrical) that an overlay builds on and that must contain the overlay's dependencies.
A lightweight, zero-overhead pub/sub protocol supported as an alternative middleware in modern ROS 2 releases for lossy wireless and edge systems.
Systematic and unfair discrimination in machine learning outputs caused by skewed training datasets, flawed model assumptions, or unrepresentative sensor validation.
A digital communication technology that served as a replacement for point-to-point wiring when connecting sensors and field devices to PLCs.
A software- and hardware-enforced virtual spatial boundary that prevents a robot or mobile platform from moving outside designated operational coordinates.
An international engineering standard outlining a structured model process for identifying and addressing ethical values and concerns throughout system design.
The annual statistical survey published by the International Federation of Robotics detailing worldwide robot shipments, operational stock, and industrial density.
A lightweight client-server publish/subscribe messaging transport protocol requiring an ordered, lossless stream of bytes over TCP ports 1883 or 8883.
A set of configurable network policies governing message reliability, durability, history, and liveliness between publishers and subscribers in ROS 2.
ABB's functional-safety option for its robot controllers; it runs on separate hardware that the RobotStudio virtual controller does not simulate.
A robot that works with or for people outside traditional manufacturing, such as a hospitality robot that greets hotel guests.
A ROS 2 QoS durability policy where the publisher retains historical messages so newly connected late-joining subscribers receive them immediately.
A circumstance where an engineer's personal, financial, or organizational loyalties could compromise or appear to bias their professional judgment.
A two-dimensional matrix barcode symbology that uses an L-shaped finder pattern and Reed-Solomon error correction to reconstruct damaged codes.
A high-fidelity virtual model of a physical robot and its environment used for simulation, offline testing, and operational monitoring.
An independent software process in ROS responsible for a single modular task, such as sensor acquisition or path planning.
The governing organization formed under OSRF in 2024 to guide the open-source development and maintenance of ROS and Gazebo.
An electromechanical actuator that technicians replace first before investigating the friction brake when repairing a faulty joint brake.
A software architecture where concurrent tasks periodically yield CPU execution by avoiding blocking delays and checking non-blocking timestamps.
A certification enforced on pull requests requiring commit messages to include a Signed-off-by line confirming the submission's origin.
The technical specification defining biomechanical pressure and force pain-onset thresholds across 29 body areas for collaborative human-robot contact.
Occupational Safety and Health Administration, the United States federal agency that investigates workplace accidents and enforces safety standards.
A RAPID error-handler instruction that runs again only the instruction that caused the error, not the whole routine.
A dedicated software bridge that translates ROS topics, services, and actions into a robot controller's proprietary communication protocol.
A recalibration procedure used when external axes lack calibration values, but not when calibration values already exist.
A Layer 2 timing and synchronization standard for time-sensitive applications specified as a profile of IEEE 1588.
Automated scripts on a USB stick that automatically back up robot programs, installation files, and configuration files.
A ROS Enhancement Proposal defining quality categories that establish differentiated standards for package versioning, testing, and documentation.
An open-source consortium initiative that extends ROS and ROS 2 capabilities to manufacturing automation and industrial manipulators.
Request-reply client-server transactions in EtherNet/IP that use TCP and are addressed to the Message Router object.
Electrical isolation established between circuits using an intermediate relay to mitigate noise interference from external equipment.
The XML manifest file defining a ROS package's metadata, maintainers, buildtool dependencies, and runtime library requirements.
A large AI model trained on huge amounts of data that can be adapted to many tasks, such as a vision-language-action model that turns images and instructions into robot actions.
The covariance representing unmodeled physical disturbances, wheel slip, and kinematic inaccuracies introduced during system motion.
A multiplier (for example 1.5 for smooth parts or 2.0 for porous ones) applied to the calculated holding force so a suction gripper keeps its grip despite acceleration and uncertainty.
